messages:
alex: Quick proposal — change admission control from immediate rejects to a tiered 'warmup/queue/degrade' flow when GPU pools saturate.
alex: Motivation: rejects spike error surface area, clients retry loudly, and some customers prefer slower responses over failures. We can get better overall throughput and predictable cost.
jamie: +1 on reducing user-visible errors. How do we avoid very long tail latencies for low-priority customers?
alex: plan is to cap queue depth per-GPU and introduce a soft-degrade where we trim KV cache & reduce kv_cache_size for degraded requests, keeping latency bounds.
nina: can we see a short config example?
alex: sure — rough draft: 
```
admit_policy:
  default: queue
  tiers:
    enterprise: degrade
    paid: queue
    free: reject_when_overflow
  queue_size_per_gpu: 120
  degrade_eviction_ratio: 0.25  # drop 25% of KV cache to save tokens
  degrade_sampling: 0.15  # only degrade 15% of paid by default
  max_queue_time_s: 3
  overflow_action: reject  # if queue full
```
nina: I like the controlled degrade + queue hybrid. we need a token-level cost model to simulate savings vs perf hit.
samir: important: clients will see 429 vs slow response. what do we expose? 429 for immediate rejects, and 202/stream with delayed tokens for queued?
lee: we should avoid inventing new status codes. suggest keeping 429 for rejects, and for queued requests respond with `queued` field in transport header + streaming when served. clients can opt-in or poll.
jamie: also need fairness: per-customer queue slots and emergency bypass for low-latency SLOs. e.g., realtime-voice customers get reserved capacity.
opsbot: capacity snapshot: 12 pools in us-west saturated 80-95% for 3h windows last week. avg queue length observed: 40 reqs/pool when under stress.
alex: rollout plan idea:
- canary 5% traffic for 24h in us-west
- telemetry: p50/p95 latency, client error rate, retry amplification, cost delta per-1k tokens
- kill switch: revert to current policy if p95 latency > +200ms or retries > 2x baseline
jamie: what about warm pools? we can keep a tiny warm pool per-customer for high-priority users. that reduces cold-starts and makes degrade less visible.
samir: warm pools cost money. need per-customer economics: reserve for top X customers only. include warm pool sizing rule in policy config.
lee: ops question: how will admission signals be emitted? existing saturations are based on gpu_util and queue_len. we should add model_seq_len_distribution to choose kernel and early-admit.
ina: experiment suggestion: sim traffic with recent week of traces and run an admission simulator to measure tail latency & token cost. I can run that if we get config vars.
alex: assigning tasks: nina -> simulator run with proposed params, jamie -> client contract for queued responses + header format, samir -> cost model and warm-pool economics, lee -> instrumentation and rollout playbook.
samir: FYI, in cost sim a 20% degrade sampling reduced token compute by ~12% in last run, with p95 latency up ~80ms for degraded subset.
jamie: don't forget telemetry on fairness: per-customer starvation metric. we should alert if any customer sees >3x drop in throughput for 10m.
opsbot: noting policy knobs in config store: `admit_policy_v2` feature-flagged. rollout toggles available.
alex: TL;DR — prefer hybrid queue + soft-degrade over wholesale rejects. less customer-visible failures, controlled perf hit, savings possible. want 👍 to start sim + spec docs.
lee: 👍 from infra side. I'll prep SRE playbook with rollback steps.
nina: I'll post the sim results in this thread by EOD tomorrow.
samir: will draft economics doc too.
jamie: I'll start an API PR for queued semantics.
alex: thanks all — will schedule sync if sim shows promise. :thumbsup:
